A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Temporal Straightening for Latent Planning. The complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, with retained content identifiable across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original goal-reaching simulations on Wall, PointMaze and PushT, including success rates in Tables 1–3 and representation and teleportation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original simulations and adds planning-cost comparisons, alternative-regularizer experiments and measured planning-time results.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 adds an optional long-horizon planning objective, L_plan = L_spatial + 0.1 L_agg, using the existing aggregation head. The encoder, predictor and principal training objectives remain unchanged; renaming the pooling head does not introduce a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions use Wall, PointMaze-UMaze, PointMaze-Medium, PushT and Teleported-PointMaze, including the existing longer-horizon tests. Teleported-PointMaze moves from Appendix E to F; the added comparisons use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds smoothness and temporal contrastive objectives, with contrastive windows k = 2 and 5, as evaluated comparators on PushT (Appendix B.5, Figure 12). This is a targeted expansion; the existing DINO-WM and GD/CEM comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: The reported planning learning rate changes from 0.01 in v1 Table 5 to 0.1 in v2 Table 4, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. New experiments also vary GD/CEM optimization budgets and temporal-regularizer strengths and windows.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends diagnostic testing: alternative temporal penalties test the specificity of straightening, budget sweeps quantify success–runtime trade-offs, and a spatial-versus-combined-cost ablation examines long-horizon planning (Figures 10 and 12; Table 2). Existing dimension, cosine-variant and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The redrawn Figure 5 removes the success-rate error bars shown in v1. Tables retain mean ± standard deviation reporting, and the stated three-data-seed practice continues. The PDFs do not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds combined-cost results, including 33.33 ± 4.16% PushT projector MPC success, while Figures 10 and 12 add runtime and alternative-regularizer findings. All existing Table 1 scores, original Table 2 rows and v1 Table 3/v2 Table 5 success-rate entries remain identical.

T1.justification: Section 5.3 defines the new composite spatial/aggregated goal cost, a limited addition to the mathematical objective specification. The linear-dynamics assumptions, straightness definitions, Hessian-conditioning bounds and cosine-proxy proofs in Section 4 and Appendix C remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims about curvature regularization, more faithful latent distances and improved gradient-based planning. The stated 20–60% open-loop and 20–30% MPC gains are unchanged. Explicit JEPA terminology and emphasis on previously reported implicit straightening clarify existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits symmetric Euclidean costs under asymmetric or irreversible dynamics and qualifies the teleportation heatmaps (Section 5.3; Figure 26). It also interprets the combined-cost results as motivation for distinct prediction and planning spaces and discusses compatibility with other regularizers.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 newly specifies a single L40S GPU, timing over 50 test trajectories and rollout-budget accounting. Appendix B.5 documents the added comparators’ positive windows and within-trajectory negatives. The planning learning-rate disclosure is revised; most existing training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Goroshin et al. (2015) and a substantial Appendix D covering local control, E2C/RCE, Koopman methods and plannable representations. It explicitly distinguishes trajectory straightening from locally or globally linear dynamics, substantially broadening and clarifying research positioning.

P1.justification: The principal section sequence and much existing prose are retained. Changes include copyediting, more explicit JEPA framing, replacing pooling-head terminology with aggregation head, reordering appendix hyperparameter and planner-comparison sections, and adding an impact statement.

P2.justification: The main text and references are extensively reformatted into a two-column conference layout. Figure 5 replaces the combined dual-axis display with bars and a scatterplot; new runtime, regularizer and aggregation-head figures are added, and Table 2 is expanded.

improvement.justification: The alternative-objective controls and measured planning-time study better support existing effectiveness and efficiency claims. Expanded research positioning and the explicit asymmetry limitation improve their interpretation and scope. These are incremental gains: benchmark coverage and theoretical guarantees remain stable, combined-cost results are mixed, Figure 5 loses error bars, and the planning learning-rate revision is unexplained.
